## SECOND instrumented occurrence the same day (2026-08-05) — closing [rebar:895c-3eb2-043a-4de1]

A second loop, captured automatically by the same shipped instrumentation, on a DIFFERENT ticket
hours after the first:

    completion-verifier, agentic, bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6
    hit step budget (request_limit=240 max_iterations=480) in 712.9s
    requests=240 tool_calls=255 distinct=74 max_consecutive_repeat=172
    top_repeats=[{search_files:e2b20f57, 175}, {search_files:65bd515d, 3},
                 {read_file:acc2bd17, 2}, {read_file:ce2c3550, 2}, {search_files:163c71be, 2}]

### Two occurrences now, and they differ usefully

| | aec1 | 895c |
|---|---|---|
| requests | 240/240 | 240/240 |
| tool_calls | 253 | 255 |
| distinct | 30 | **74** |
| distinct ratio | 0.119 | **0.290** |
| worst single signature | 222x | 175x |
| max_consecutive_repeat | 217 | 172 |
| wall clock | 753.6s | 712.9s |

**The ratio moved (0.119 -> 0.290) while the outcome did not.** That matters for
[rebar:70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0]'s actuator: a trip threshold set too tight would have caught aec1 and
MISSED this one. 70bc's proposed `<= 0.50` catches both, with the healthy control at 1.000 — so the
proposed threshold has now been exercised against two real pathological runs at different ratios,
not one.

**Both tickets are small.** aec1: no descendants, 4 declared files. 895c: no descendants, 4 declared
files. Neither is an epic. Combined with e369 (59 descendants), the loop occurs across the whole size
range — **scale is not the trigger**. The common shape is one `search_files` query re-issued to
exhaustion (222x and 175x), which points at the agent failing to make progress on a search that
returns nothing useful, not at breadth of work.

**Both were fully delivered.** 895c's fix is MERGED to `origin/main` (`d8adf0f5654`) through
`LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`, with a certified plan-review attestation, a held-out RED->GREEN
oracle proven by two defect-seeded mutations, and an end-to-end replication showing the original
report no longer reproduces. It still could not close through the gate. Both tickets were
force-closed with the evidence recorded.

**That is now four force-closes traceable to this one defect** (e369, aec1, 895c, plus the earlier
history this ticket documents). Each one is a ticket that met its bar and could not say so through
the gate — the trap this ticket exists to remove.
